title: Hezbollah Chief: Iran-US Deal Is Best Chance to End Israeli Aggression in Lebanon
detail: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem stated that a potential Iran-US nuclear and security deal represents the best opportunity to end Israeli 'aggression' in Lebanon, signaling the group's negotiating posture ahead of the May 14-15 Washington talks between Israel and Lebanon mediated by the United States. The statement indicates Hezbollah is tying its own ceasefire terms to the broader Iran-US diplomatic track, suggesting the Washington negotiations will be closely linked to the parallel nuclear diplomacy. Israeli military operations have continued throughout, killing over 2,750 people and displacing more than 1.2 million since March 2.

media.caption: Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem links Iran-US deal to ending Israeli operations in Lebanon

title: 10 Killed in Israeli Strikes Including Two Paramedics, Lebanon Health Ministry Confirms
detail: Lebanon's Health Ministry confirmed that at least 10 people were killed in Israeli strikes, including two paramedics among the casualties — the latest in an ongoing wave of Israeli military operations across Lebanon. The BBC reported the deaths of the medical personnel alongside civilian casualties, highlighting continued risks to humanitarian workers operating in strike-affected areas. Israeli airstrikes have persisted despite US diplomatic pressure ahead of the May 14-15 Washington talks, raising serious concerns about the protection of civilians and medical staff under international humanitarian law.

media.caption: Lebanese paramedics among 10 killed in Israeli strikes as Washington talks approach
